title: The scalar counit equation for the transported composite chart
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$, and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, and choose $N=\ell^n\geq1$ annihilating both. On either the ordinary etale or pro-etale site let $\mathcal C_{T,R}=D^b_{ctf}(T,R)$ mean the full category of constant-$R$ module complexes with bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude: tensor with any degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology in one fixed finite interval [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer]. Write $T_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The finite Tate line is $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$ on the etale site and its comparison inverse image on the pro-etale site; $(d)$ denotes tensor with its $d$th tensor power [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist].
Let $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_Y$ be separated etale of finite type, $g=p_de$, and choose standing compactifications. Use $F^{et}_{g,R}\dashv H^{et}_{g,R}$ and $F^{pro}_{g,R}\dashv H^{pro}_{g,R}$ with their specified sum-then-ordered-affine counits as constructed in [lem-sp-chart-finite-ring-adjunction], for $R=A,B$. On either site the natural isomorphism
$$a_{g,K}:T_UH_{g,A}K\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{g,B}T_YK$$
is the canonical derived tensor/pullback, shift and Tate identification [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback, det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]; on the Tate line it sends $(z\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $z\otimes\varphi(a)b$. Let $\beta_g$ on the etale site and $b_g$ on the pro-etale site be the specified compact-support coefficient maps [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. For every $K\in\mathcal C_{Y,A}$, the actual composite chart counits satisfy
$$\epsilon^{et}_{g,B,T_YK}\circ F^{et}_{g,B}(a_{g,K})\circ\beta_g(H^{et}_{g,A}K)=T_Y(\epsilon^{et}_{g,A,K}),$$
and
$$\widetilde\epsilon_{g,B,T_YK}\circ F^{pro}_{g,B}(a_{g,K})\circ b_g(H^{pro}_{g,A}K)=T_Y(\widetilde\epsilon_{g,A,K}).$$
These equations use the specified fixed-compactification maps and remain true after canonical refinement identifications. They concern the explicit chart right functor and its counit, without assuming an exceptional coefficient comparison invertible or choosing any smooth orientation.

source.place: Charts: paste the two coefficient-counit equations, identify the fixed left map, and transport; retained Steps 7--11

proof.text:
Put $V=\mathbf A^d_Y$, $E_R=De_{\Sigma!,R}$, $h_R=e_R^*$, $P_R=F_{d,R}$ and $G_R=p_{d,R}^*(-)(d)[2d]$. Write $u_R$ and $v_R$ for the affine and sum counits. The chart adjunction has right functor $h_RG_R$ and composite counit $w_R=u_R\circ P_R(v_R G_R)$ before its left comparison. The cited domain statement puts $G_AK$, $h_AG_AK$, all compact-support values and their scalar extensions in the required finite-Tor categories. The canonical chart tensor map is
$$a_g=h_B(a_d)\circ a_e(G_AK).$$
Indeed the pullback/tensor maps on a K-flat representative carry $x\otimes b$ to the pullback of $x$ tensored with $b$; the Tate factor on either path carries $(z\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $z\otimes\varphi(a)b$. The shift is even, so no interchange sign occurs. The domain statement also identifies this map through site comparison.

source.place: Charts: domains, canonical right-functor comparison and sum-then-affine counit

proof.text:
Apply the two scalar-counit statements with base $Y$ for $p_d$ and with input $G_AK$ for $e$. They give
$$u_{B,T_YK}P_B(a_d)\beta_d(G_AK)=T_Y(u_{A,K}),$$
$$v_{B,T_VG_AK}E_B(a_e(G_AK))\sigma_e(h_AG_AK)=T_V(v_{A,G_AK}).$$
Both use the specified coefficient maps; the second input is allowed by Step 1. These statements require neither flatness nor finite projective dimension of $B/A$.

source.place: Charts: the affine and etale-sum coefficient-counit equations

proof.text:
For an object $M$ on $U$ set $s_M=P_B(\sigma_e(M))\beta_d(E_AM)$. Suppress object subscripts when their type determines them. Expanding $w_B$ and $a_g$, naturality of $v_B$ at $a_d:T_VG_AK\to G_BT_YK$ gives
$$w_BP_BE_B(a_g)s_{h_AG_AK}
=u_BP_B\bigl(a_d\,v_{B,T_VG_AK}E_B(a_e(G_AK))\sigma_e(h_AG_AK)\bigr)\beta_d(E_Ah_AG_AK).$$
The sum equation of Step 2 replaces the three middle factors by $T_V(v_{A,G_AK})$. Naturality of $\beta_d$ at $v_{A,G_AK}$ then gives
$$u_BP_B(a_d)\beta_d(G_AK)\,T_Y(P_A(v_{A,G_AK}))=T_Y(u_A)T_Y(P_A(v_AG_A))=T_Y(w_A),$$
where the affine equation of Step 2 was used. This is a direct substitution and naturality calculation, not an extra geometric comparison.

source.place: Charts: paste the two scalar-counit equations

proof.text:
Let $\lambda_R:P_RE_R\xrightarrow{\sim}F^{et}_{g,R}$ be the cited graph-normalized comparison. Its statement gives both $\epsilon^{et}_{g,R}=w_R\lambda_R(h_RG_R)^{-1}$ and
$$\beta_g\,T_Y(\lambda_A)=\lambda_BT_U\,s.$$
Precompose the desired etale equality with the isomorphism $T_Y(\lambda_A(h_AG_AK))$. The left side becomes, by this square and naturality of $\lambda_B$ at $a_g$,
$$\epsilon^{et}_{g,B}F^{et}_{g,B}(a_g)\lambda_B(T_Uh_AG_AK)s=w_BP_BE_B(a_g)s.$$
Step 3 makes this $T_Y(w_A)$, which equals $T_Y(\epsilon^{et}_{g,A})T_Y(\lambda_A(h_AG_AK))$. Cancel the common invertible precomposition. This proves the asserted equation for the actual etale counit and the named $\beta_g$.

source.place: Charts: identify the fixed left map, preserving its actual counit

proof.text:
For an etale object $L$ on $Y$, abbreviate site comparison by $C_{T,R}$, its tensor comparison by $\delta_T$, and the fixed compact-support comparison by $c_R=c_{g,R}$. Put $M=H^{et}_{g,A}L$ and $M'=H^{et}_{g,B}T_YL$. The chart-adjunction statement gives $\widetilde\epsilon_R=C_{Y,R}(\epsilon^{et}_R)c_R^{-1}$ on comparison objects. The coefficient/site square gives, at $M$,
$$F^{pro}_{g,B}(\delta_{U,M})b_g(C_{U,A}M)=c_B(T_UM)C_{Y,B}(\beta_g(M))\delta_{Y,F^{et}_{g,A}M}\,T_Y(c_A(M))^{-1}.$$
The domain statement intertwines the geometric right functors and their tensor comparisons. Thus after identifying $H^{pro}_{g,A}C_{Y,A}L$ with $C_{U,A}M$, the map $H^{pro}_{g,B}(\delta_{Y,L})a^{pro}_g$ is $C_{U,B}(a^{et}_g)\delta_{U,M}$. These are the specified comparisons, not a choice of right-adjoint orientation.

source.place: Charts: specified transported counit and coefficient/site square

proof.text:
Postcompose the proposed pro-etale equation at $C_{Y,A}L$ with $\delta_{Y,L}$. Naturality of the B-counit first replaces its target by $C_{Y,B}T_YL$ and inserts $F^{pro}_{g,B}(H^{pro}_{g,B}(\delta_{Y,L}))$. Substitute the formulas of Step 5. Naturality of $c_B^{-1}$ at $a_g^{et}:T_UM\to M'$ cancels $c_B(T_UM)$, leaving
$$C_{Y,B}\bigl(\epsilon^{et}_{g,B}F^{et}_{g,B}(a_g^{et})\beta_g(M)\bigr)\delta_{Y,F^{et}_{g,A}M}\,T_Y(c_A(M))^{-1}.$$
Step 4 replaces the parenthesized factor by $T_Y(\epsilon^{et}_{g,A})$. Naturality of $\delta_Y$ turns the result into
$$\delta_{Y,L}\,T_Y\bigl(C_{Y,A}(\epsilon^{et}_{g,A})c_A(M)^{-1}\bigr)=\delta_{Y,L}\,T_Y(\widetilde\epsilon_{g,A}).$$
Cancel $\delta_{Y,L}$. This proves precisely the equation with the named $b_g$ on every etale-origin object.

source.place: Charts: explicit cancellation in transport of the counit identity

proof.text: Every pro-etale $K$ in the stated category is isomorphic to $C_{Y,A}L$ by the comparison equivalence in the chart-adjunction statement. All factors of the equation are natural transformations (the canonical tensor comparisons, coefficient maps and counits). Applying their naturality to this isomorphism and cancelling it proves the equation at $K$. For refinement $c\to c'$, write $\phi_R:F^c_{g,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}F^{c'}_{g,R}$. The refinement clause gives $q^{c'}T_Y(\phi_A)=\phi_BT_U q^c$, with $q=\beta$ or $b$. Under the canonical adjunction identification the counit is $\epsilon^{c'}=\epsilon^c\phi_R(H_R)^{-1}$. Substitution, naturality of $\phi_B$ at $a_g$ and cancellation of $\phi_B$ show that the equation for $c'$ is the equation for $c$ precomposed with $T_Y(\phi_A(H_A))^{-1}$. Common-refinement comparisons obey the same clause, so the assertions hold after their canonical identifications as well.

tool_uses.why: Uses its specified coefficient/site square and refinement equations to transport the actual counit; the chart unit does not itself provide these compact-support coherence squares.

Its K-flat computation of the canonical tensor/pullback comparison justifies checking the factorization on the representing tensor maps; this general ringed-topos construction is not supplied by a chart-unit node.
